objective: Investigate small unexplained velocity changes reported during some Earth gravity-assist flybys.

observations.observation: Precise orbit reconstructions for some Earth gravity-assist flybys show small discrepancies between pre-flyby and post-flyby asymptotic velocity estimates.
The effect is extremely small relative to the spacecraft's overall velocity and requires precise tracking to detect.
The anomaly has been reported for multiple spacecraft/flybys, including Galileo, NEAR, and Rosetta cases discussed in the literature.
Other Earth flybys, including a well-tracked later case, have not shown the same anomalous velocity change.
The reported effect depends on comparing extremely precise tracking data with gravitational-assist trajectory models.
Candidate explanations discussed for such discrepancies include conventional modelling/measurement effects and hypotheses involving unmodelled physical effects.
The supplied evidence does not identify a single mechanism that quantitatively explains every reported and null case.

constraints: Do not force a definitive explanation.
Separate empirical correlations from causal explanations.
Consider tracking, atmosphere, Earth orientation, gravity modelling, spacecraft properties, and other conventional systematics before exotic physics.
If the evidence remains insufficient, identify the measurement or experiment that would discriminate among hypotheses.
